name: fema-mcp-server
what_it_holds: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server / API client exposing FEMA OpenFEMA endpoints: disaster declarations, public-assistance grants, individual/household housing aid, and NFIP flood-insurance claims. Actively maintained TypeScript project (docs/, tests/, CI, package.json), last updated 24 Aug 2026, Apache-2.0.
why_useful: Turns FEMA's official disaster-declaration and NFIP flood-claims feeds into a clean, scriptable pull for gap 11 (hurricanes/wildfires/floods as shocks to specific STR markets) and could be repointed to pull county-level declarations timed against Airbnb market calendars.
size_hint: small (source code only, no committed data)
time_coverage: current OpenFEMA API coverage (1953-present per OpenFEMA)
themes: Weather, hurricanes, wildfires, disasters: NOAA/NHC tracks, EM-DAT, FEMA declarations, wildfire perimeters (Maui, LA fires), heatwaves; tourism-shock datasets
why_all: Turns FEMA's official disaster-declaration and NFIP flood-claims feeds into a clean, scriptable pull for gap 11 (hurricanes/wildfires/floods as shocks to specific STR markets) and could be repointed to pull county-level declarations timed against Airbnb market calendars.

One-command programmatic pull of the same OpenFEMA declaration + assistance + NFIP-claims data as the rearc mirror, but live and queryable, including NFIP flood claims which give a dollar-loss proxy per county/disaster not in the plain declarations file.

name: catastrophe-risk-dashboard

name: Earth-Engine-Wildfire-Data
what_it_holds: Python toolkit for downloading, processing, and preparing wildfire perimeter data from Google Earth Engine (GEE), supporting both historical and forecasted wildfire datasets; generates config files for wildfire modeling workflows. MIT licensed, 4 stars, updated 22 Nov 2025.
why_useful: A scriptable, non-Airbnb-site method to pull historical wildfire perimeters (could target Maui 2023 and LA Jan 2025 fires specifically) for gap 11 tourism-shock timing/severity, more current than static NIFC/GeoMAC dumps.
size_hint: code only, pulls data on demand from GEE
geography: global (wherever GEE fire products cover, incl. US)
themes: Weather, hurricanes, wildfires, disasters: NOAA/NHC tracks, EM-DAT, FEMA declarations, wildfire perimeters (Maui, LA fires), heatwaves; tourism-shock datasets
why_all: A scriptable, non-Airbnb-site method to pull historical wildfire perimeters (could target Maui 2023 and LA Jan 2025 fires specifically) for gap 11 tourism-shock timing/severity, more current than static NIFC/GeoMAC dumps.

name: datacenters-wildfires
what_it_holds: Interactive map site combining US data-center locations with historical wildfire perimeters (NIFC/WFIGS, 2016-Sep 2026) per its description. Directory listing shows only `us_data_centers_100mw_plus.csv` and an HTML map committed; wildfire perimeter data itself is pulled live from the NIFC/WFIGS API, not stored in-repo. Updated 10 Sep 2026 (very fresh).
why_useful: Confirms NIFC/WFIGS as a live, current (through Sep 2026) wildfire-perimeter API worth querying directly for gap 11 (Maui/LA fires and any 2026 wildfire events); the repo itself is not a data store but demonstrates a working integration pattern.

name: noaastormevents (CRAN mirror)
what_it_holds: Read-only GitHub mirror of the CRAN R package `noaastormevents`, an R client for exploring NOAA's Storm Events Database (1950-present: tornadoes, hurricanes/tropical storms, floods, hail, high wind, wildfire, heat, etc., county-level with property/crop damage estimates).
why_useful: Gives a clean, maintained R interface to the authoritative NOAA county-level storm-events feed (hurricanes, wildfires, heatwaves all included as event types) for gap 11; could be used to build a county-to-STR-market crosswalk for shock timing/severity.
